title: A polynomial algorithm for general d-position in trees
summary: A vertex set is in general $d$-position if no three of its vertices lie on a shortest path of length at most $d$. We give an exact algorithm for an $n$-vertex tree in $O(n(D+2)^4)$ time and $O(n(D+2)^2)$ space, where $D=\min\{d,n-1\}$. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when the threshold is part of the input. This answers the tree-complexity question posed by Klav\v zar, Rall, and Yero in 2021 and retained in the August 2026 version of the general position survey.
